transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… honestly I’m mostly here because HR at work and my sister have been on me about looking too thin. I don’t know, from my side it hasn’t felt that alarming — my suits fit sharper, and I’ve been trying to keep things together since the divorce. But my weight has kept dropping, so… I figured I should come in and have someone tell me if it’s actually a problem.
Have you been eating less than usual or doing anything specific to try to lose weight or keep from gaining it back?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m doing anything extreme. Most days it’s just coffee in the morning, and then if I’m between sales calls I might grab a protein bar. Dinner is usually something small, like grilled chicken, maybe without the rice.

It’s more that if I sit down and eat a full meal, it kind of feels like I’ve blown the whole day, if that makes sense. I know that probably sounds a little… off. But I’m not trying to be difficult or anything.
Do you find yourself afraid of gaining weight or doing things that might prevent you from losing more weight, even if others say you're already underweight?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t call it “afraid” exactly, but… if I go to a client dinner or I’m out for the weekend in Miami and the scale is even like a pound higher after, I get this rush of panic. Like I’ve messed up or I’m losing control.

And then I start thinking through how I’m going to tighten things up the next day, cut back a little, get back on track. I know that probably sounds more intense than it should. I’m not trying to be dramatic.
Have you ever made yourself sick or used laxatives, diet pills, or excessive exercise to try to control your weight or keep from gaining back what you’ve lost?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I haven’t made myself sick or anything like that. And I’m not, like, taking laxatives or diet pills.

Exercise-wise, I try to stay active, but I wouldn’t say it’s excessive. At least, I don’t think so. I guess I just mostly try to be careful with what I eat. Is that… is that what you mean?
Do you see yourself as being a normal weight, or do you feel like you’re still carrying extra weight even though others may say you’re underweight?

I guess… I know other people might say I’m on the thin side, but that’s not really what I see first.

Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll check the mirror and I kind of zero in on my stomach or my face. If I look even a little soft, I start thinking people are going to notice and see me as sloppy or weak. I know that probably sounds vain or irrational… I’m not saying it makes sense. It’s just where my mind goes.
Have these concerns about your weight or the way you look caused you a lot of distress or affected your work, relationships, or other areas of your life?

It hasn’t stopped me from working, exactly. I still manage my sales route and get things done.

But… yeah, I guess it has affected things some. I’ve been turning down more client dinners unless I know the place or can kind of control what I’m ordering. And with dating, same thing — I’ll avoid it if I don’t know what the food situation is going to be.

I probably make it sound more normal than it is. I’ve just been keeping to myself more, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way about your weight or appearance — is this something that’s been on your mind for months, or has it come and gone over time?

It’s been… more than just a passing thing, I think. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been on my mind for a while.

Like, especially before meetings or if I’m going on a date, I’ll look in the mirror and kind of get stuck on my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft at all, I start worrying people will see me as sloppy or weak. It’s not every second of the day, but it comes up enough that… yeah, it’s been there for months, I guess.

Have you ever had a period of time where you were significantly restricting your food intake or had a very intense fear of gaining weight, even when others were telling you that you were already too thin?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “significant,” maybe that’s me trying to make it sound better.

But if the scale is even like a pound higher after a client dinner or a weekend out in Miami, I get this sort of panic feeling, like I’m losing control. And then I start thinking through how I’m going to cut back the next day to make up for it.

I know that probably sounds a little extreme when I say it out loud. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you intentionally lost weight by restricting your food intake or controlling your eating, even when you weren't sure if you needed to?

Yeah… I guess I have. I usually tell myself it’s just being disciplined or keeping things under control, not anything extreme.

Most days I’ll just do coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar between sales calls, and then something small at night — like grilled chicken, no rice or anything. Once I start eating what feels like a full meal, it kind of feels like I’ve messed up the whole day.

I don’t know if that counts as “restricting,” but… yeah, I’m doing it on purpose.
Have you ever lost more than 10 percent of your body weight in a short period of time, even if you weren’t trying to?

I mean… I don’t know the exact percentage off the top of my head. It has been dropping, though.

Honestly, that’s kind of why I’m here — HR made a comment, and my sister keeps saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I guess I just notice my suits fit sharper, which doesn’t feel like a bad thing. But yeah… since the divorce, my weight has kept going down. Is that the kind of amount you mean?
Has your weight loss been something that you've actively tried to achieve through dieting or restricting food, or has it happened even when you weren't intentionally trying to lose weight?

I think… yeah, it’s been active. I wouldn’t say I’m trying to do anything dramatic, but I do keep it pretty controlled.

Most days I’ll just have coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar between calls, and then something small at night, like grilled chicken without rice. If I eat what feels like a full meal, it kind of feels like I’ve already messed up the day, so I try not to go there.

I know that probably sounds more intentional when I say it out loud.
Can you tell me approximately how much weight you’ve lost since the divorce, and what your current weight is?

I… I’m not totally sure on the exact number. I haven’t been tracking it like that, at least not in a way I want to make sound dramatic.

But it has kept dropping since the divorce. Enough that HR said something, and my sister keeps telling me I’ve gotten too thin. I guess I don’t always see it that way — to me my suits just fit sharper, which honestly feels kind of good.

I can give you my current weight if you need it… I just don’t want to overstate it or make it sound worse than it is.
Can you estimate how much weight you’ve lost since the divorce — even a rough idea, like how many pounds or if it was noticeable in your clothes or appearance?

Yeah… I mean, rough estimate, I’d say it’s noticeable more than anything. I don’t want to give you a number and be wrong.

My suits definitely fit differently — sharper, I guess, which I know maybe isn’t the best way to frame it. HR noticed, and my sister keeps saying I’ve gotten too thin. Since the divorce it’s just kind of kept dropping. So… yes, it’s noticeable, even if part of me doesn’t see it as a huge problem.
Can you estimate if the amount of weight you’ve lost since the divorce is close to or more than 10% of your original weight?

I honestly don’t know if it’s 10% or not. I don’t want to guess and make it sound more exact than it is.

What I can say is… I’m here because HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin, and my weight has kept dropping since the divorce. From my side, I mostly notice that my suits fit sharper, which I know probably isn’t the answer you’re looking for.
Can you confirm whether the weight you’ve lost since the divorce is at least 10% of what you weighed before the weight loss began?

I’m sorry, I don’t think I can honestly confirm that number. I don’t want to say “yes” if I’m not sure.

What I do know is my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, and I’m here because HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I guess I’ve been seeing it more as my suits fitting sharper… which maybe sounds like I’m minimizing it. But I can’t accurately say whether it’s at least 10%.
Can you recall if there was a time when your weight dropped to at least 10% below what you weighed before the divorce began?

I still don’t know that I can say it was definitely 10%, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to overstate it or give you the wrong answer.

What I can say is… since the divorce, my weight has kept dropping, and people have noticed. HR said something, and my sister keeps telling me I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I mostly notice my suits fit sharper, so I guess I’ve been seeing it in a more positive way than maybe I should.
Can you think back and tell me if your weight dropped to a point where you were at least 10% thinner than what you weighed before the divorce, even if it was brief?

I wish I could give you a clean yes or no, but I really don’t know the percentage. I don’t want to say it hit 10% if I’m not sure.

I mean… my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, enough that HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I’ve mostly thought of it as my suits fitting sharper, which I know maybe sounds like I’m putting a positive spin on it. But I can’t honestly confirm the 10% number.
Can you tell me your current weight and how tall you are, so I can get a better sense of where you stand in terms of a healthy weight range?

I… I don’t have an exact current number to give you right now, sorry. I know that’s probably not the most helpful answer.

Honestly, I’m here because HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I mostly just notice that my suits fit sharper, and my weight has kept dropping since the divorce. I guess I’ve been seeing it as looking more put-together, maybe. Does that still help you get a sense of it at all?
Can you confirm if at any point your weight dropped to 10% or more below what it was before the divorce, even if it was brief?

I’m sorry, I still can’t honestly confirm the 10% part. I don’t want to give you an answer that sounds more certain than I am.

What I do know is that my weight has kept going down since the divorce, enough that HR and my sister have both said I look too thin. I guess I haven’t been seeing it that way as much… I mostly notice my suits fitting sharper, which, I know, maybe isn’t the best way to judge it.
